Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide

Prolabs Robotics. FTC Intake Upgrade Kit, for a goBILDA FTC robot with a hex shaft intake, 2026-27. Detailed assembly steps only.
Finished intake
FTC intake attachment
The kit has 1 FTC intake attachment and foam. Wrap the foam until it reaches the POLLEN, then test with a real POLLEN.
Created by: Aarav J.
Collaborators: R-Factor FRC

7 steps, 14 sub-steps.

Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide | Page 1 of 13

Before you start

In the picturesMeaning
Dark part: the part you add or move in this step
Mid grey: foam that is already wrapped
Light grey part: already on the robot, do not touch
Black arrow: move the part this way
Dashed circle: look here
Close-up boxA zoomed view of the same step
The POLLEN decides when to stop wrapping. The foam should just touch the POLLEN and give it a light squeeze. Always test with a real POLLEN at the real intake height.

Directions. Front means the side of the robot where the POLLEN comes in. Left and right are as seen from the front. All sizes are in mm. The POLLEN is 2.8 in (about 71 mm) across.

Your robot may look different. The side plates and motor in the pictures are simple shapes. Use the hex shaft, bearings and collars already on your intake.

Hex shaft. The attachment has a 7 mm hex hole (across flats). Check that your intake shaft fits before you start.

Checklist

1a Sort the parts
1b Check the print
2a Slide the attachment onto the hex shaft
2b Centre it and lock it
3a Start the foam
3b Make the first wrap
4a Keep wrapping, layer by layer
4b Stop when the foam reaches the POLLEN
5a Check the fit with a POLLEN
5b Add or take off a layer
6a Zip tie the foam
6b Tape the ends (optional)
7a Spin test
7b Final check

Kit contents

PartQtySizeNotes
FTC intake attachment1180 mm long, 30 mm across, 7 mm hex hole3D print, 100% infill, about 150 g
Foam1 sheet180 mm wideWrapped around the attachment until it reaches the POLLEN
Zip ties1 bag2.5 mm wide4 used to hold the foam. The rest are spares

One robot uses 1 attachment, enough foam to reach about 50 mm across (your POLLEN check decides), and 4 zip ties.

Tools and things you need

ToolUsed for
Hex key for your shaft collarsTaking the shaft out and locking the attachment
Scissors or a sharp knifeCutting the foam to 180 mm wide and cutting the end
Flush cuttersTrimming zip tie tails
Ruler (mm)Measuring the foam and checking the print
Tape (any)Holding the start of the foam, and the ends (optional)
1 POLLEN ballThe fit check in step 5
Fine sandpaperOnly if the hex hole is tight
Adults should handle the knife. Cut away from your hands.

Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide | Page 4 of 13
1aSort the partsStep 1 of 7: Lay out the kit
Take the parts out of the kit and put them on a clean table.
Parts1 FTC intake attachment, 1 foam sheet, zip ties
Size and positionAttachment: 180 mm long, 30 mm across, 7 mm hex hole
Which wayAny
TipKeep the foam flat. Do not fold it or cut it yet.
Close-up: the 7 mm hex hole
1bCheck the printStep 1 of 7: Lay out the kit
Look at both ends and along the full length. The part must be straight and solid, with no gaps or loose strings in the hex hole.
Size and positionLength 180 mm. Diameter 30 mm. Hex hole 7 mm across flats, all the way through.
Which wayLook down the hex hole from one end. You should see light from the other end.
TipStand the part on the life size circle on page 4 to check the size. It is printed at 100% infill, so it should feel heavy, about 150 g.
Side view: 180 mm long
Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide | Page 5 of 13
2aSlide the attachment onto the hex shaftStep 2 of 7: Mount the attachment
Take the intake hex shaft out of one side of the robot, or loosen it. Slide the attachment onto the shaft.
Parts1 FTC intake attachment
ToolsThe hex key for your intake shaft collars
Which wayEither end first. Both ends are the same.
TipIf the shaft is tight, lightly sand the flats inside the hole. Do not make it loose, or it will spin on the shaft.
Close-up: the shaft going into the hex hole
2bCentre it and lock itStep 2 of 7: Mount the attachment
Put the shaft back in its bearings. Move the attachment to the centre of the intake. Lock it with the shaft collars or spacers already on your robot.
Size and positionSame gap on both sides, between the attachment and the side plates.
Which wayThe attachment must not slide along the shaft.
TipSpin the shaft by hand. It should turn freely and the attachment should turn with it, with no slipping.
Close-up: shaft collar at the end
Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide | Page 6 of 13
3aStart the foamStep 3 of 7: Start the foam wrap
Cut the foam to the same width as the attachment, 180 mm. Lay the first edge of the foam along the full length of the attachment and hold it with 3 short pieces of tape.
PartsFoam, tape (not in the kit, any tape is fine here)
Size and positionFoam width: 180 mm, the same as the attachment. Keep the foam edge straight along the part.
Which wayStart the foam on the side that faces you.
TipMake sure the foam does not stick out past the ends. It can rub on the side plates.
3bMake the first wrapStep 3 of 7: Start the foam wrap
Turn the shaft the same way the intake spins. Let the foam wrap around the attachment. Pull it gently so it sits tight with no air gaps.
Size and positionOne full turn is one layer.
Which wayWrap in the same direction the intake spins. Then the loose end of the foam trails behind and does not peel open.
TipKeep the foam edges in line with the ends of the attachment on every turn.
Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide | Page 7 of 13
4aKeep wrapping, layer by layerStep 4 of 7: Build up the layers
Keep turning and wrapping. Each new layer goes straight on top of the last one. Keep the same gentle pull every time.
Size and positionGrow the diameter slowly. About 50 mm across is a good place to stop and test.
Which waySame direction as step 3b.
TipDo not stretch the foam hard. Stretched foam gets thin and loses its grip.
Close-up: end view of the layers
4bStop when the foam reaches the POLLENStep 4 of 7: Build up the layers
Hold one POLLEN on the floor in front of the intake. Keep adding layers until the foam just touches the top of the POLLEN.
Parts1 POLLEN ball (2.8 in)
Size and positionThe foam should reach the POLLEN at the height your intake sits.
Which wayCheck in the middle and at both ends of the attachment.
TipDo not cut the foam yet. Hold the loose end with your hand or one piece of tape until the fit check is done.
Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide | Page 8 of 13
5aCheck the fit with a POLLENStep 5 of 7: POLLEN fit check
Roll one POLLEN slowly into the intake. Turn the shaft by hand. The foam should touch the POLLEN, grip it, and pull it in.
Parts1 POLLEN ball
Size and positionThe foam squeezes the POLLEN a little, about 2 to 3 mm. A light squeeze, not a hard push.
Which wayRoll the POLLEN in from the front, the way it will come in during a match.
TipTry the POLLEN at the left, the centre and the right of the intake.
The foam just touches the POLLEN
5bAdd or take off a layerStep 5 of 7: POLLEN fit check
Use this table. Change one layer at a time and test again.
TipWhen the fit is good, cut the foam so the end sits flat. Cut it straight across, along the full 180 mm.
What you seeWhat to do
The POLLEN rolls under the foam and is not pulled inAdd one more layer of foam
The foam touches but slips on the POLLENAdd half a layer, or pull the last layer tighter
The POLLEN gets stuck, or the motor slows down a lotTake off one layer
The foam is thick on one end and thin on the otherUnwrap and wrap again, keeping the edges in line
The POLLEN comes in with a light squeezeGood. Go to step 6
Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide | Page 9 of 13
6aZip tie the foamStep 6 of 7: Secure the foam
Put 4 zip ties around the foam, spread along the length. Pull each one tight enough to hold the foam, but not so tight that it cuts deep into it.
Parts4 zip ties
Size and positionAbout 25 mm and 75 mm from the centre on each side. Keep the last tie 10 to 15 mm in from each end.
Which wayPut one zip tie over the loose end of the foam so it cannot open.
TipCut the tails flush. Turn the zip tie heads so they sit in different places around the roller, not all in one line.
Close-up: one zip tie, tail cut flush
6bTape the ends (optional)Step 6 of 7: Secure the foam
If the foam ends lift up, wrap one turn of tape around each end of the foam.
PartsTape (not in the kit)
Size and positionAbout 15 mm wide, at each end of the foam.
Which wayWrap the tape the same way the intake spins.
TipPut the zip ties on first, then the tape. Keep tape off the middle of the foam, where it touches the POLLEN.
Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide | Page 10 of 13
7aSpin testStep 7 of 7: Test
Run the intake motor at low power, then full power. Feed in POLLEN one at a time.
Size and positionWatch the foam. It must stay tight and must not wobble or rub the side plates.
Which wayThe intake must pull the POLLEN in, not push it away. If it pushes away, reverse the motor in your code.
TipStop the motor at once if anything comes loose.
7bFinal checkStep 7 of 7: Test
Check every part one last time before you drive.
CheckAttachment locked, no slipping on the shaft. Foam tight, no loose end. 4 zip ties tight, tails cut. Nothing rubs the side plates.
TipCheck the foam after every few matches. Foam wears down. Add a layer when the grip gets weak.
Intake Upgrade Assembly Guide | Page 11 of 13

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat happens, and the fix
Printing the attachment with low infillIt can crack around the hex hole. Always print at 100% infill.
Hex hole too tight, so you hammer the shaft inThe part can split. Lightly sand the flats inside the hole instead.
Hex hole sanded too muchThe attachment spins on the shaft and does not grip. Print a new one.
Attachment not locked with collarsIt slides along the shaft and rubs a side plate. Lock it in step 2b.
Wrapping the foam the wrong wayThe loose end lifts and peels open when the intake spins. Wrap the same way the intake spins.
Too much foamThe POLLEN gets stuck and the motor slows down or stalls. Take off one layer.
Too little foamThe POLLEN rolls under the intake and is not pulled in. Add one layer.
Foam wider than 180 mmIt rubs on the side plates. Trim it flush with the ends.
Stretching the foam hardIt gets thin and loses grip. Use a gentle, even pull.
Zip ties too tightThey cut deep grooves in the foam and the POLLEN catches on them. Pull just tight enough to hold.
Zip tie tails left longThey hit the POLLEN and the robot. Cut them flush.
Tape over the whole foamTape is slippery and the POLLEN slides. Only tape the ends.
Skipping the POLLEN fit checkThe intake may work on the table but not on the field. Always test with a real POLLEN at the real intake height.
Not checking the foam during the eventFoam wears and gets loose. Check it after every few matches.
If the intake does not pull the POLLEN in, go back to step 5 and test again with a real POLLEN.
